title: Best Grow Room Dehumidifier (2026): Cannabis & Hydro Picks
h1: The Best Grow Room Dehumidifiers, Sized by Plants and Water
dek: Nearly every gallon you pour into a pot ends up in the air. A grow room dehumidifier is how you take it back out.
description: The best grow room dehumidifier for your space: cannabis dehumidifiers sized by daily watering, LGR and ducted picks, humidity by stage and drying-room tips.
intro: A **grow room dehumidifier** has a harder job than a basement unit. Plants return most of the water you give them to the air, so a spare bedroom full of healthy plants can add gallons of moisture a day, right as flowering calls for drier air. This guide is for growers who've moved past a single tent to a whole room, whether that's houseplants, vegetables, hydroponic greens or cannabis where it's legal. Three things matter most: enough capacity for the water you put in, a design that keeps pulling at the 40–50% humidity late growth calls for, and hands-off drainage. Our top pick, the **AlorAir Storm Elite**, nails all three for a typical mid-size room.

For a smaller room, the **AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S** adds Wi-Fi alerts at lower capacity, and the **Waykar 158-Pint Dual Duct** connects by ducting so its heat stays outside the room. Cultivation laws vary by state and country; this page covers environmental control only, and its humidity figures are general horticulture guidance.
topPicksLead: The **AlorAir Storm Elite** is our top grow room dehumidifier because its LGR design keeps removing water at flowering humidity levels, it pumps its own drainage and it has the headroom for a room full of plants.

blocks.text: Put together, the math is simple: water in roughly equals moisture out. Pour 6 gallons a day and the room must shed close to 48 pints of vapor, plus evaporation from soil, trays and reservoirs.

sections.heading: How we pick grow room dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We compared rated capacity and the conditions behind each rating (AHAM, saturation or a brand's own test), drainage, ducting, low-humidity performance, controls and power draw, then read manuals, extension-service guidance on indoor growing humidity and owner reviews from growers. We don't lab-test units ourselves; every capacity figure is the maker's rating.

sections.heading: How big a dehumidifier for a grow room?

blocks.text: Square footage barely matters here. What sizes a grow room dehumidifier is how much water goes in. Use this simple grow room dehumidifier calculator:

items: **Add up daily watering** in gallons, including nutrient solution. Subtract any runoff you collect and remove from the room.
**Multiply by 8** to get pints of moisture per day.
**Add 10–25%** for open reservoirs, wet floors and evaporation from trays, more for hydroponic rooms.
**Compare against the AHAM rating**, and add more headroom if your unit is rated at saturation or you're targeting the low 40s.

sections.heading: How to choose a grow room dehumidifier

items.label: Size by water, then add headroom
items.text: Start from the calculator above. A unit running flat out all day can't catch up after lights-off.

items.label: Choose LGR if you flower
items.text: Standard compressor units lose much of their output below about 50% humidity. Low-grain refrigerant units are designed to keep working there, which is where late flower lives.

items.label: Plan for the heat
items.text: A dehumidifier puts out its own power draw as heat, plus the heat released when vapor turns to water. In a sealed room, your AC has to remove that too, or you can duct the unit outside the room.
sub: Our guide to [how much electricity a dehumidifier uses](/guides/how-much-electricity-does-a-dehumidifier-use/) helps estimate the load

items.label: Insist on a pump or a drain
items.text: A grow room dehumidifier may pull several gallons a day. Bucket models will stop when full, often in the middle of the night.

items.label: Use a separate hygrometer
items.text: Built-in sensors read humidity at the machine. A [good hygrometer](/best/best-hygrometer/) at canopy height tells you what the plants actually experience.

items.label: Count your circuits
items.text: Lights, fans, pumps and AC already load the room. Keep each 15-amp circuit under about 12 amps of continuous draw and give big units their own outlet.

items.label: Keep the filter clean
items.text: Perlite dust and plant debris clog intakes fast and cut capacity; check the filter every week or two.

blocks.title: Watch the lights-off spike
blocks.text: When lights switch off, the room cools and relative humidity jumps even though no extra water was added. Set the dehumidifier to run through that window and check your hygrometer's history for overnight peaks.

sections.heading: Using a dehumidifier for drying cannabis and herbs

blocks.text: Drying is a different job from growing. Where it's legal, most guidance calls for a dark, cool space around 60–70°F at roughly **55–62% humidity** for a week or two, so material dries evenly. A big grow room unit is usually too much; a small unit with a precise humidistat, or the HYDRONE 7, works better.

items: Use a separate room, closet or tent, not the active grow room.
Keep fans pointed at walls, not directly at hanging material.
Check humidity twice a day early on, when the most moisture is released.

blocks.text: Our [drying room dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-drying-room/) guide covers setup, curing ranges and the right small units in detail.

Inside is simplest: set the unit low, a foot or more from walls and plants, where room fans move air past it. In sealed rooms with AC, outside is better, because the unit's heat stays out; duct humid air to it and dry air back, as with the Waykar or a [ducted dehumidifier](/best/best-ducted-dehumidifier/).
A hydroponic dehumidifier also has to handle evaporation from reservoirs and channels. Lidded reservoirs and covered trays cut that load noticeably.
Run a pump line or hose to a floor drain, sink or container and check it each visit; a kinked hose on a high-capacity unit can flood a floor overnight.

items: **A mid-size room with a full canopy in flower:** the AlorAir Storm Elite.
**A spare bedroom or basement corner with a few plants:** the AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S, with Wi-Fi alerts.
**A sealed room with AC where heat is the problem:** the Waykar 158-Pint Dual Duct, installed outside the room.
**A large veg room or hydroponic setup on a budget:** the Kesnos 150-Pint, remembering its rating is optimistic.
**A closet grow or a separate drying space:** the AC Infinity HYDRONE 7.
**Still growing in tents?** Start with our [grow tent dehumidifier](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-grow-tent/) picks, and step up to a room unit when you outgrow them.

blocks.text: Size a grow room dehumidifier by the water you pour in, not the square footage, and favor a design that keeps working at flowering humidity. For most rooms, buy the **AlorAir Storm Elite**. Go smaller with the **Sentinel HDi65S**, ducted with the **Waykar 158-Pint Dual Duct**, cheaper with the **Kesnos 150-Pint** and compact with the **AC Infinity HYDRONE 7**, and confirm the room with a hygrometer at canopy height.

faqs.q: What size dehumidifier do I need for a grow room?
faqs.a: Multiply your daily watering in gallons by 8 to get pints of moisture, add 10–25% for evaporation, then choose a unit whose AHAM rating covers that with room to spare. A room watered with 6 gallons a day needs roughly 50–60 pints of real capacity.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for a cannabis grow room?
faqs.a: For most mid-size rooms, the AlorAir Storm Elite. Its LGR design keeps removing water at the 40–50% humidity flowering calls for, and its built-in pump handles drainage. Smaller rooms suit the AlorAir Sentinel HDi65S.

faqs.q: Is a commercial dehumidifier worth it for a grow room?
faqs.a: Usually, once you're past one or two tents. Household units are built for basements and fade at flowering targets; commercial and LGR units handle heavy, continuous loads and drain automatically.

faqs.q: Can I use a regular dehumidifier in a grow room?
faqs.a: For a small room or veg-only space, a household 50-pint unit with a pump or drain hose can work. In a full room in flower, it will often run nonstop without reaching 40–50%, so an LGR or commercial unit is the better buy.

faqs.q: Should I use a dehumidifier when drying cannabis?
faqs.a: Where it's legal, a small dehumidifier helps hold a drying space at about 55–62% humidity and 60–70°F. The goal is slow, even drying, so set a target rather than running it at full power. See our drying room guide for setup details.

faqs.q: Where should a dehumidifier go in a grow room?
faqs.a: Low in the room, a foot or more from walls and plants, where fans move air past it. In sealed rooms with AC, a ducted unit outside the room keeps its heat out of the grow space.
